=== NOTES 1:206 | Revolutionary Nationalism – Anushilan Samiti, Yugantar, Alipore and Kakori-era Cases, Savarkar
## SUB 0 | Anushilan Samiti and Yugantar – Bengal
[206:0:0] # Anushilan Samiti
[206:0:1] - **Founded 1902, Calcutta**, by **Pramathanath (P.) Mitra** with **Satish Chandra Basu**; named after Bankim's *Anushilan Tattva*; associated with Aurobindo, Barindra Ghosh, Bipin Pal.
[206:0:2] - A **secret revolutionary society** – trained youth for armed struggle; dacoities, bombs, assassinations = **militant nationalism through revolutionary acts** (not social reform, women or labour welfare).
[206:0:3] - **Barindra Kumar Ghosh** (Aurobindo's younger brother) – his activities built its revolutionary core; head of the secret society in the Alipore case.
[206:0:4] - **Dhaka Anushilan (1906):** **Pulin Behari Das** – outgrew the Calcutta parent; organised the **Barrah dacoity (1908)** in Dhaka district = the **first major venture of the revolutionaries in East Bengal**, to raise funds.
[206:0:5] - **Sachindranath Sanyal:** joined Anushilan (1907); exam keys: set up its **Patna branch (1913)**; with Rash Behari Bose in the Hardinge bomb (1912).
[206:0:6] - **Tripura** was drawn into the movement early in the 20th century because **Bengal revolutionaries took shelter there**.
[206:0:7] # Yugantar (Jugantar)
[206:0:8] - **Weekly started April 1906** by an Anushilan inner circle – **Barindra Kumar Ghosh, Bhupendranath Dutta** (and Abinash Bhattacharya).
[206:0:9] - **Bhupendranath Datta** (Vivekananda's brother) stood before the British as **Yugantar's editor** and was jailed for sedition (1907).
[206:0:10] - The western Anushilan under **Jatindranath Mukherjee (Bagha Jatin)** emerged as the **Yugantar party**; German Plot (1915); Jatin died at **Balasore, September 1915**.
[206:0:11] > Anushilan = **P. Mitra 1902**; Dhaka branch = **Pulin Das**; Yugantar paper = **Barindra + Bhupendranath**; Yugantar party = **Bagha Jatin**.
[206:0:12] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.316-318; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.73-74, 169; NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 6 p.72, 77; Wikipedia "Bhupendranath Datta"
## SUB 1 | Abhinav Bharat, Mitra Mela and V.D. Savarkar
[206:1:0] TABLE head: Body | Founder | Place, year
  [206:1:0.0] Mitra Mela | V.D. Savarkar with brother Ganesh (G.D.) | Nasik, 1899 – merged into Abhinav Bharat, 1904
  [206:1:0.1] Abhinav Bharat (Young India Society) | V.D. Savarkar and G.D. Savarkar | Nasik, Maharashtra, 1904 (exam stems say 1905); named after Mazzini's Young Italy
  [206:1:0.2] Indian Republican Army | Surya Sen | Chittagong, 1930
  [206:1:0.3] Hindustan Republican Association | S.N. Sanyal (with Bismil, Jogesh Chatterjee) | Kanpur, 1924
[206:1:1] - **Abhinav Bharat** killed **A.M.T. Jackson**, Collector of Nasik (1909, Anant Kanhere) → **Nasik conspiracy case**: Savarkar – life in the **Andamans**.
[206:1:2] - **Savarkar abroad:** went to **London in 1906** to study law and carried Abhinav Bharat's work there (India House).
[206:1:3] - **All four true (RAS 2013):** founded Abhinav Bharat; wrote a **biography of Mazzini**; wrote **"The Indian War of Independence, 1857"** (1909) – the nationalist view of 1857; **jumped from the ship at Marseilles (1910)** to escape, but was recaptured.
[206:1:4] > Abhinav Bharat / Mitra Mela = **Savarkar** (not Khudiram, Bhagat Singh, Tilak or C.R. Das).
[206:1:5] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.318; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.72; PMF Modern History Part 3 (Indian War of Independence); NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 6 p.72-73
[206:1:6] - Savarkar's **Hindutva** was published in **1923**.
## SUB 2 | Early Actions – Phadke, Chapekars, Muzaffarpur
[206:2:0] # Maharashtra
[206:2:1] - **Vasudev Balwant Phadke (1879):** organised **Ramosi peasants** into a force (the "**Ramosi Krishak Jatha**") – an **armed uprising in the 1870s**; the first revolutionary activity in Maharashtra; crushed.
[206:2:2] - **Chapekar brothers** (Damodar and Balkrishna, Tilak's disciples) shot **Plague Commissioner W.C. Rand** and Lt. Ayerst, **Poona, 1897**.
[206:2:3] # Muzaffarpur bomb (April 1908)
[206:2:4] - **Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki** bombed a carriage at **Muzaffarpur (Bihar)** meant for Judge **Kingsford**; two British ladies died; **Chaki shot himself**, **Khudiram was hanged**.
[206:2:5] > Phadke = **Ramosis, 1879**; Rand = **Chapekars, 1897**; Kingsford = **Muzaffarpur, 1908**.
[206:2:6] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.316, 318; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.71-73
[206:2:7] - The Chapekars' attack was a protest against the **excesses of plague control** (house searches) under Rand.
[206:2:8] - Vanchi Aiyar's act (1911) was linked to **V.O. Chidambaram Pillai's** Swadeshi Steam Navigation agitation.
[206:2:9] - Vanchi Aiyar belonged to the **Bharata Matha Association** (Madras Presidency).
[206:2:10] - **Vanchi Aiyar** (Bharata Matha Association, linked to V.O. Chidambaram Pillai's Swadeshi Steam Navigation agitation) shot Collector **Robert Ashe** at **Maniyachi railway station**, 17 June 1911.
## SUB 3 | Alipore and Delhi Conspiracy Cases
[206:3:0] # Alipore (Maniktala) conspiracy case, 1908
[206:3:1] - After Muzaffarpur the whole Anushilan group was arrested – **Aurobindo and Barindra Ghosh**; called the Manicktolla or Muraripukur conspiracy.
[206:3:2] - **Chittaranjan Das defended Aurobindo** → acquitted; Barindra and Ullaskar Dutt – death, commuted to life.
[206:3:3] # Delhi conspiracy case – Hardinge bomb, 1912
[206:3:4] - **23 December 1912:** bomb at **Viceroy Hardinge** in **Chandni Chowk** during his state entry into Delhi – injured, not killed.
[206:3:5] - **Mastermind:** **Rash Behari Bose** (with **Sachin Sanyal**); bomb thrown by **Basanta Kumar Biswas**; organisation credited: **Anushilan Samiti** (UPPCS 2023) – not Yugantar.
[206:3:6] - Executed: **Master Amir Chand**, Avadh Behari, Bal Mukund, Basanta Biswas; Rash Behari escaped to **Japan**.
[206:3:7] # Cases → revolutionaries (RAS 2021)
[206:3:8] TABLE head: Case | Revolutionary
  [206:3:8.0] Howrah (Howrah-Sibpur) conspiracy, 1910 | Jatindranath Mukherjee
  [206:3:8.1] Lahore conspiracy | Rajguru (with Bhagat Singh)
  [206:3:8.2] Delhi conspiracy, 1912 | Master Amir Chand
  [206:3:8.3] Alipore conspiracy, 1908 | Aurobindo Ghosh
[206:3:9] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.316-317; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.73-74; NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 6 p.78; Wikipedia "Delhi conspiracy case"
[206:3:10] - Trigger: police raid on the **Maniktala** bomb factory (Muraripukur Road), Calcutta.
[206:3:11] - **49** were accused in the Alipore case (19 sentenced).
[206:3:12] - **Order:** Rand killed (1897) → Muzaffarpur bomb and Khudiram's execution (1908) → Curzon Wyllie killed in London (1909) → Hardinge bomb (1912).
[206:3:13] - Approver **Narendranath Goswami** was shot inside the jail by **Kanailal Dutta** and **Satyendranath Bose**.
## SUB 4 | Revolutionary Press and Organisations
[206:4:0] - **Sandhya** and **Yugantar** (Bengal) and **Kal** (Maharashtra) advocated revolutionary action – **all three**.
[206:4:1] - **Bandi Jivan** ("A Life of Captivity", 1922) – **Sachindranath Sanyal**, written in the Cellular Jail.
[206:4:2] - **Revolutionary bodies:** **Abhinav Bharat** and **Anushilan Samiti**. Not revolutionary: the **(United) Indian Patriotic Association (1888)** – Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and Raja Shiv Prasad, to oppose the Congress; "New Nationalist Party".
[206:4:3] TABLE head: Paper | Founder / editor
  [206:4:3.0] Yugantar (1906) | Barindra Kumar Ghosh, Bhupendranath Dutta
  [206:4:3.1] Sandhya (1906) | Brahmabandhab Upadhyay
  [206:4:3.2] Bande Mataram (Calcutta) | Bipin Chandra Pal; edited by Aurobindo
  [206:4:3.3] Mukti Kon Pathe (1906) | Barindra Kumar Ghosh (manual)
[206:4:4] - **Bharat Mata Society** = **Ajit Singh, Punjab** – not Bengal.
[206:4:5] - **Background:** first phase rose after the Surat split and Swadeshi repression; weakness – never a **mass movement**; Aurobindo's pamphlet **Bhawani Mandir (1905)**.
[206:4:6] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.318, 878; NextGen Indian History APPSC Part 6 p.72, 77; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.71, 169
